inspect.description: Read Google's stored index state for one URL under the property; not a live fetch

get_sitemap.description: Read one sitemap under the property

create_file.description: Creates an empty Google Doc, Sheet, Slides deck, or folder. kind document, spreadsheet, presentation, and folder map to application/vnd.google-apps.document, spreadsheet, presentation, and folder.

upload_file.description: Uploads bytes to Drive as a multipart file and imports them as a Google type unless convert is false. Text, Markdown, HTML, and Word become a Doc, CSV, TSV, and Excel become a Sheet, and PowerPoint becomes Slides. Exactly one of content and content_base64 is accepted, content is only for the five text types, and content_base64 must decode to the bytes it claims.

move_file.description: Moves a Drive file into folder_id by reading the file's parents, then adding the folder and removing the parents that read returned. These are two calls, so a parent added between them stays.

create_event.description: Creates a calendar event, asking Google to email guests only when notify_guests is true. start and end are each a YYYY-MM-DD date or an RFC 3339 date-time; given together they must be the same kind, and an all-day end is exclusive. A date-time with no offset needs an IANA time_zone such as America/Denver, never a bare offset, and time_zone is accepted only with start or end. Google, not this connector, refuses an end that is not after start. notify_guests defaults to false and is sent as sendUpdates all or none; none asks Google not to email guests, which Google does not fully promise, and Google warns that guests outside Google Calendar may then not receive the event. calendar_id refuses a dot, a double dot and any slash. An attendee address follows the Gmail address rule, at most 254 characters and 254 bytes.

update_event.description: Patches only the given fields of a calendar event, replaces the attendee list when attendees is sent, and clears the date or date-time a changed start or end leaves behind. At least one of summary, description, location, start, end and attendees is required. start and end are each a YYYY-MM-DD date or an RFC 3339 date-time; given together they must be the same kind, and an all-day end is exclusive. A date-time with no offset needs an IANA time_zone such as America/Denver, never a bare offset, and time_zone is accepted only with start or end. Google, not this connector, refuses an end that is not after start. notify_guests defaults to false and is sent as sendUpdates all or none; none asks Google not to email guests, which Google does not fully promise, and Google warns that guests outside Google Calendar may then not receive the event. calendar_id refuses a dot, a double dot and any slash. An attendee address follows the Gmail address rule, at most 254 characters and 254 bytes.

create_draft.description: Saves a message in Gmail Drafts and does not send it. Each recipient item is a single plain address with no display name, group or comment, at most 254 Unicode code points and 254 UTF-8 bytes. All input strings must be well-formed Unicode; lone surrogates are refused. Supply thread_id, in_reply_to and references together or omit all three. The last references entry must equal in_reply_to, the immediate parent's RFC Message-ID, not its Gmail resource id; match the parent's Message-Id header name from get_message case-insensitively. References are the ordered ancestor IDs including that parent last, at most 20 entries of at most 254 ASCII characters each; excluded Message-ID forms and longer ancestry must be reported, never rewritten or truncated. Google requires threadId to identify the existing thread, RFC 2822 compliant References and In-Reply-To, and matching Subject headers. Supply the existing subject unchanged; no Re: is added and no lookup verifies the thread, account, subject or parent. To/Cc/Bcc and RFC 2047 UTF-8 subjects are folded; text leaves use standard base64 wrapped at 76 characters and raw uses unpadded base64url. Local attachments require the local stdio gateway and 1 to 10 regular files totaling at most 2097152 bytes, counting duplicate paths once per occurrence. Omit attachments for no files. The gateway checks native absolute paths, actual byte sizes and integrity, refusing protected paths, environment files, memory ancestry, links including linked ancestors, multiply linked files, unreadable files and changes since approval; supply a real path. The module uses only prepared bytes, checks their count, metadata, length and SHA-256, and attaches them in the order the gateway prepared them, which is input order. Unknown extensions use application/octet-stream without content sniffing. With files MIME is multipart/mixed, body first, then attachments in input order; body_html, including empty HTML, makes a nested multipart/alternative. Attachment filenames use escaped ASCII or RFC 2231 UTF-8 parameters. No local path enters MIME. File bytes never appear in results; only selected Gmail resource fields are returned. A failed or malformed response is never automatically retried.

attachments.description: Absolute paths on the local stdio gateway only. At most 10 regular files, totaling at most 2097152 bytes per message. Omit this field for no attachments; an empty array is invalid. The gateway screens protected paths, links, identities and changes since approval before giving private bytes to the module. See the action description for filesystem refusals.

send_draft.description: Send this saved draft only with the person's explicit go for this message. This action always asks for confirmation and cannot use a standing approval. The saved draft may have changed in Gmail since it was composed. The stop shows the draft id; it does not preview or bind remote draft bytes. Supply the Draft id, not a Message id. Sends the saved To/Cc/Bcc without a lookup, replacement message or retry, returning only selected Message resource fields.

standing_approval.caution: This grant sends messages your assistant writes, to any recipient, with no look at each one before it is sent. It never covers a message with a local file attached.

update_values.description: Overwrites one spreadsheet range. value_input_option defaults to RAW, so text that begins with an equals sign is stored as text unless the caller asks for USER_ENTERED, and each cell must be a string of at most 5000 characters, a number, or a boolean, in 1 to 500 rows of 1 to 50 cells, and a range of . or .. is refused.

append_values.description: Inserts rows at the end of a spreadsheet table with insertDataOption INSERT_ROWS and does not overwrite cells below the table. value_input_option defaults to RAW, so text that begins with an equals sign is stored as text unless the caller asks for USER_ENTERED, and each cell must be a string of at most 5000 characters, a number, or a boolean, in 1 to 500 rows of 1 to 50 cells, and a range of . or .. is refused.

create.description: Creates an empty Google Doc with the given title.

edit.description: Applies one ordered all-or-nothing batch of insert, replace, paragraph style, and list operations to a Google Doc. insert_text without an index writes at the end of the body, end_index must be greater than start_index, match_case defaults to true, bulleted maps to BULLET_DISC_CIRCLE_SQUARE and numbered to NUMBERED_DECIMAL_ALPHA_ROMAN, and required_revision_id is sent as writeControl.requiredRevisionId so an edit against a stale revision is refused. In a document with tabs, replace_text changes every tab and the indexed operations act on the first tab.
